title: Connect a business bank account so invoices can be paid by bank transfer

icp.label: Early stage SaaS founders
icp.description: Founders of 2 to 10 person B2B SaaS teams who do their own bookkeeping.

task.goal: Connect a business bank account so invoices can be paid by bank transfer

success.criterion: Bank account shows as connected in billing settings

factors.label: Trust and willingness to share
factors.lowAnchor: Refuses to give personal data or payment until value is proven
factors.whyItMattersHere: Connecting a bank means handing over account numbers and a phone code, and this ICP is wary of sharing before it works.

factors.label: Bank details readiness
factors.lowAnchor: Starts the connection and stops to hunt for routing and account numbers
factors.highAnchor: Has every bank detail ready and finishes in one pass
factors.whyItMattersHere: Founders who must look up routing numbers mid flow stall at the bank form.

factors.label: Patience
factors.lowAnchor: Abandons at the first real obstacle
factors.whyItMattersHere: The bank sign in can fail, and impatient founders quit at the first error.

factors.label: Product familiarity
factors.lowAnchor: Never used this product or category
factors.highAnchor: Expert in this category and similar tools
factors.whyItMattersHere: Bank connection vocabulary (routing, ACH, micro deposits) confuses first timers.

recommendations.title: Earn trust before asking for personal data
recommendations.whatToChange: Move the phone, card or account request after the moment of value, or say right next to the field why it is needed and what happens to it.
recommendations.why: Low trust and willingness to share reduced completion: Low trust founder completed 0 of 3 against 3 of 3 for the baseline (99% likely lower completion); they hit F2 (Phone verification code is required before the bank account connects).
recommendations.expectedEffect: removes a give up trigger for low trust users

recommendations.title: Cut the obstacles on the main path
recommendations.whatToChange: Fix the error that repeats, shorten the flow, and give a clear retry or alternative when a step fails.
recommendations.why: Low patience reduced completion: Impatient founder completed 1 of 3 against 3 of 3 for the baseline (93% likely lower completion); they hit F1 (Bank sign in fails with a temporarily unavailable error).
recommendations.expectedEffect: keeps impatient users going past the first obstacle

recommendations.title: Make the flow work for users with low bank details readiness
recommendations.whatToChange: Look at where Unprepared founder stalled (Routing number field gives no hint where to find the number) and remove that obstacle.
recommendations.why: Low bank details readiness reduced completion: Unprepared founder completed 1 of 2 against 3 of 3 for the baseline (86% likely lower completion); they hit F3 (Routing number field gives no hint where to find the number).
recommendations.expectedEffect: lifts completion for users at the bank details readiness risk pole

answers.question: Where do founders hesitate during bank connection?
answers.answer: Hesitation was most frequent on the verification page (5 of 10 hesitation steps). The closest finding is F4, The help article uses ACH without explaining it (hit by Novice founder, severity minor). Most runs that gave up stopped on the form page (5 abandonment(s)). Trust and willingness to share is the factor most likely to lower completion: 0 of 3 against 3 of 3 (99% likely lower completion, supported).

answers.question: Does the phone verification step cost us connections?
answers.answer: The closest finding is F2, Phone verification code is required before the bank account connects (hit by Baseline founder, Low trust founder, Stress: low trust, unprepared, impatient, novice, severity major). Most runs that gave up stopped on the form page (5 abandonment(s)). Trust and willingness to share is the factor most likely to lower completion: 0 of 3 against 3 of 3 (99% likely lower completion, supported).

icpRead: For Early stage SaaS founders trying to connect a business bank account so invoices can be paid by bank transfer, the journey is robust to product familiarity but fragile to trust and willingness to share, patience and bank details readiness: 4 of 6 archetypes dropped at least once, most often at the form step. The strongest drop off moment is bank sign in fails with a temporarily unavailable error (F1). Validate next with real users: Early stage SaaS founders who are low on trust and willingness to share (refuses to give personal data or payment until value is proven).
